newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast heavy crudes follow postings lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast heavy crudes follow postings lower.

text.p: U.S. West Coast heavy crudes fell midday Monday, as California oil companies lowered postings and scrambled to resell three force majeured cargoes of the grade, traders said.
Texaco, which owned the largest number of turned-back barrels, was applying for an emergency crude exporting permit, traders said.
"In three to four weeks, (Texaco's) crude ought to be out of here," a trader said, adding the company was stuck with about 30,000 of the 40,000 barrels-per-day cancelled.
In response to oversupply, Mobil and Chevron cut heavy crude prices by 50 cents a barrel Friday.
In the meantime, refiners were trying to run as much heavy as possible or ship barrels east on All-American pipeline.
"Texaco will go as heavy as they can. They're got the biggest incentive," the trader said.
Prices for Kern River heavy grade ranged $17 to 17.25 a barrel on Monday.
Meanwhile, crude traders shrugged off a weekend explosion at Paramount's Los Angeles refinery, noting the plant was too small to impact crude supplies.
In light crude markets, Alaskan grade firmed slightly as gasoline futures led NYMEX crude higher Monday.
Outright prices were $22.70/22.90 a barrel, with the differential holding at $1.45 under WTI.
ANS buyers bid around $2.00 a barrel under March WTI and saw the next deal done around $1.60 a barel.
